knowledge:
- key_parameters: alg=The clustering algorithm of choice (e.g., "louvain", "lec", "wt", "fc", "infomap", "sgG1", "sgG2", "sgG5") ;; N=Number of randomization rounds in makeConsensusMatrix (at least 500 recommended for real analysis) ;; type=Sampling scheme in makeConsensusMatrix (1 to sample edges, 2 to sample vertices) or random graph model in getRandomGraphCentrality (e.g., "cgnp") ;; mask=Percentage of edges or vertices to mask in makeConsensusMatrix ;; reclust=Logical indicating whether reclustering should be performed on the community set found ;; Cnmax=Maximum cluster size above which reclustering is performed ;; permute=Permutation type in calcDiseasePairs (e.g., "r") ;; Nperm=Number of permutations for significance testing in runPermDisease ;; alpha=Significance threshold in runPermDisease and clusterORA ;; col=Collapse parameter in clusterORA (e.g., COLLAPSE)
- alternatives: Cytoscape and Network Analyst are mentioned as preferred tools for direct network reconstruction, whereas BioNAR is preferred for detailed topologically-based network analysis of pre-existing networks. For clustering, multiple algorithms are supported as alternatives to Louvain ("louvain"), including Leading-Eigenvector ("lec"), Walktrap ("wt"), Fast-Greedy ("fc"), InfoMAP ("infomap"), and SpinGlass ("sgG1", "sgG2", "sgG5").
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a list of proteins and their interactions (or a pre-built network) and want to quantify the topological properties of the network, identify functional modules/communities, find key "bridging" proteins that connect different functional modules, and evaluate the overlap and statistical significance of disease-associated or functionally-associated gene sets within the network.
- pitfalls: Downstream functions require non-empty GeneName attributes, so users must check and resolve any NA values (e.g., using any(is.na(V(gg)$GeneName))) before proceeding. Consecutive invocations of the same clustering algorithm can produce slightly different community structures due to internal random initialization; users should use calcClustering or calcAllClustering to store memberships consistently as vertex attributes. Using too few randomization rounds (e.g., N=5 in makeConsensusMatrix or Nperm=100 in runPermDisease) is common for quick testing but insufficient for robust statistical inference (at least 500 rounds are recommended).

workflows.name: ppi_network_analysis_pipeline
workflows.intent: Build, annotate, and analyze a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network to identify central proteins, functional communities, bridging proteins, and disease/annotation overlaps.
input: PPI_Presynaptic.csv (tabular edge list with columns entA, entB, We)
flatfile_human_gene2HDO.csv (disease annotation file mapping genes to Human Disease Ontology terms)
workflows.stages: 1. Build the network from a data frame or load a predefined graph. ;; 2. Annotate vertices with gene names, diseases, and functional annotations. ;; 3. Estimate vertex centrality measures (degree, betweenness, clustering coefficient, semilocal centrality, mean shortest path, page rank, standard deviation of shortest path). ;; 4. Fit degree distribution to power law and estimate entropy rate. ;; 5. Perform community detection (clustering) and evaluate modularity. ;; 6. Recluster dense communities and visualize. ;; 7. Build consensus matrix and evaluate cluster robustness. ;; 8. Calculate and plot bridgeness. ;; 9. Analyze disease/annotation pair overlaps and calculate significance. ;; 10. Perform cluster overrepresentation analysis (ORA).
workflows.code:
file <- system.file("extdata", "PPI_Presynaptic.csv", package = "BioNAR")
tbl <- read.csv(file, sep="\t")
gg <- buildNetwork(tbl)
gg<-annotateGeneNames(gg)
any(is.na(V(gg)$GeneName))
afile<-system.file("extdata", "flatfile_human_gene2HDO.csv", package = "BioNAR")
dis <- read.table(afile,sep="\t",skip=1,header=FALSE,strip.white=TRUE,quote="")
gg <- annotateTopOntoOVG(gg, dis)
sfile<-system.file("extdata", "SCH_flatfile.csv", package = "BioNAR")
shan<- read.table(sfile,sep="\t",skip=1,header=FALSE,strip.white=TRUE,quote="")
sgg<-annotateSCHanno(gg,shan)
ggGO <- annotateGOont(gg)
gg <- calcCentrality(gg)
mc <- getCentralityMatrix(gg)
pFit <- fitDegree( as.vector(igraph::degree(graph=gg)),threads=1,Nsim=5, plot=TRUE,WIDTH=2480, HEIGHT=2480)
ent <- getEntropyRate(gg)
SRprime <- getEntropy(gg, maxSr = NULL)
plotEntropy(SRprime, subTIT = "Entropy", SRo = ent$SRo, maxSr = ent$maxSr)
nm<-normModularity(gg,alg='louvain')
alg = "louvain"
mem <- calcMembership(gg, alg)
gg <- calcClustering(gg, alg)
mem.df<-data.frame(names=V(gg)$name,membership=factor(V(gg)$louvain))
lay<-layoutByCluster(gg,mem.df,layout = layout_nicely)
remem<-calcReclusterMatrix(gg,mem.df,alg,10)
lay<-layoutByRecluster(gg,remem,layout_nicely)
conmat <- makeConsensusMatrix(gg, N=5, alg = alg, type = 2, mask = 10,reclust = FALSE, Cnmax = 10)
clrob<-getRobustness(gg, alg = alg, conmat)
br<-getBridgeness(gg,alg = alg,conmat)
gg<-calcBridgeness(gg,alg = alg,conmat)
g<-plotBridgeness(gg,alg = alg, VIPs=c('8495','22999','8927','8573', '26059','8497','27445','8499'), Xatt='SL', Xlab = "Semilocal Centrality (SL)", Ylab = "Bridgeness (B)", bsize = 3, spsize =7, MainDivSize = 0.8, xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = 0, ymax = 1, baseColor="royalblue2", SPColor="royalblue2")
p <- calcDiseasePairs( gg, name = "TopOnto_OVG_HDO_ID", diseases = c("DOID:10652","DOID:3312"), permute = "r" )
r <- runPermDisease( gg, name = "TopOnto_OVG_HDO_ID", diseases = c("DOID:10652","DOID:3312"), Nperm = 100, alpha = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001) )
ora <- clusterORA(gg, alg, name = 'TopOnto_OVG_HDO_ID', vid = "name", alpha = 0.1, col = COLLAPSE)
